commits.message:
chore(ci,email-parsing): add regression suite as a GitHub check, strip security-gateway banners

Scoped from a cross-check of an uploaded "production use-case catalogue"
doc against what's actually implemented -- most of it turned out to
already be built (LLM fallback is live, idempotency is DB-backed and
multi-instance-safe via idempotency_keys' INSERT ... ON CONFLICT,
providers are configured, quoted-history/forwarded-header/disclaimer
stripping and multi-requirement splitting and field-level provenance
all already exist). One of its claims was actively wrong for this
deployment (section 39: hermes-api/hermes-postgres/hermes-graph-consumer
all correctly share the auto-derived hermes_default network; the
intelligence_intelligence_net it named belongs to an unrelated service,
and RabbitMQ is reached over a Tailscale IP, not Docker networking, so
there's no cross-network dependency to fix). Two things it flagged did
turn out to be real gaps -- this commit is those two.

CI (.github/workflows/hermes-regression.yml): the 17-script regression
suite has been run by hand before every deploy all session -- now it
also runs as a required GitHub check on every push/PR to main, against
a real ephemeral Postgres service container, so a change that breaks
parsing/dedupe/taxonomy/review can't reach main without a human
choosing to override a failing check. A second job type-checks and
builds the frontend (tsc -b && vite build) the same way it's been
manually verified before each deploy this session. HERMES_LLM_FALLBACK_
ENABLED/HERMES_PROMPT_RUNTIME_DRY_RUN are set but never exercise a real
LiteLLM call -- hermes-850-email-llm-fallback-check.py mocks
run_llm_fallback entirely by design (see that script's own docstring),
so CI needs no real credentials.

Security-gateway banner stripping (app/email_parsing/parsers.py): every
corporate email gateway (Microsoft Defender, Proofpoint, Mimecast) tags
externally-sourced mail with a banner ("[EXTERNAL]", "CAUTION: This
email originated from outside the organization...") -- and recruiter/
vendor mail is external by definition, so this shows up on a large
share of real inbound requirements. Left unstripped it was the same
class of bug the jobs.nvoids.com relay preamble was: sitting right at
the top of the body, exactly where a title/company guess looks first.
Added _SECURITY_BANNER_LINE_PATTERN alongside the existing forwarded-
header and vendor-preamble patterns in _strip_forwarded_header_block,
matched generically on phrasing rather than one vendor's exact wording
since Defender/Proofpoint/Mimecast don't share an exact template.

New coverage: test_security_gateway_banner_is_stripped in
hermes-850-email-parsing-check.py. Full regression suite (17 checks)
green against a freshly built image and freshly reset schema.

Deliberately NOT touched from the same doc, with reasoning:
- attachment parsing (XLSX/CSV hotlists, PDF/DOCX resumes/JDs): a real
  gap (ChannelAttachment exists as a model, nothing parses one yet) but
  a large build with no confirmed evidence yet of how much of Jobfynder's
  actual inbound mail is attachment-based versus body-text -- worth
  scoping deliberately, not guessing at.
- candidate application/submission parsing, requirement update/closure
  intents, hotlist update semantics, multi-tenant ownership resolution:
  enterprise ATS scope with no evidence in this session's real
  production data (which has been 100% job_description/hotlist plain-
  text vendor-relay mail) that Jobfynder receives these email shapes
  today.
- Req ID/Job ID extraction as a near-duplicate signal: no confirmed
  example yet of a real Jobfynder posting using one.
